text: made of soul. A fluffy young fox with a curious nose was sniffing some flowers and striking pose. When out from the forest there thundered a sound. A lion came roaring and shaking the ground. The fox jumped back and dove behind bark. His tail went stiff and his eyes

Grew dark. Oh goodness, he gasped. What a beast I have found. That roar could rattle the roots from the ground.  But days went by and they met once more. The lion just strolling, not quite as sore. The fox still trembled, but not quite as much, though he flinched at the roar and stayed out of touch. The whistling me soft call and respond. Face the growl, the grom, the glare. You might just find there's nothing there.

And then one morning, clear and bright, the fox walked up with zero fright. He puffed out his chest and waged his tail and said, "Why like that? What's the tail?  The lion blinked and scratched his man. He looked a bit confused and plain. He didn't pounce. He didn't shout. He simply watched the fox walk out.
Now don't assume this tail means go and tease all beasts you barely know. Some lions bite and some do not. It mostly just depends a lot.
